items.text: I will try to hear THIS mantra.
items.source: HG Bhurijana Prabhu, Melbourne 2006 japa workshop

items.text: This name — I will hear it.
I will catch the first 'Hare'.
items.source: Bhurijana 2006 — 'the most important word… is the first one'

items.text: I cannot focus, but I will sit. The attempt is the practice.
items.source: Bhurijana 2006 — 'just make the attempt, make the saṅkalpa'

items.text: I will chant humbler than the straw, more tolerant than the tree, offering respect, expecting none.
I will not retaliate today — even within my mind — so the Name can act.
Today I will not just pronounce — I will call out.
Today I will reform my tendency to remain absent during chanting.
Today I will serve Kṛṣṇa within while my tongue chants without.
I will accept the Name as Kṛṣṇa Himself — chanting is meeting, not recitation.
When the mind rebels, I will neglect it and return to the Name.
Brahma-muhūrta is here. I will not let it pass without offering rounds.
If I missed brahma-muhūrta, I will not skip — I chant now.
Today is Ekādaśī. I will complete my rounds before noon.
Today I chant to Kṛṣṇa as my master. I will address Him in that mood.
Taste is not the test today. Attention is. I will attend, regardless of taste.
I will not wait for purity to begin. I begin in spite of impurity — that IS the purification.
I will not demand sixteen. I will request one. Then one more.
items.source: The 'just one more' principle — HG Bhurijana Prabhu

items.text: If I wander, the next mantra is the same fresh chance. I begin again, now.
items.source: BG 6.26; Bhurijana 2006 — 'the same chance on the next mantra'

items.text: Let my last conscious thought tonight be Your Name.
items.source: BG 8.6 (anta-kāle ca mām eva); Prahlāda's example (SB 7.5)
